baking-soda-deodorant.text: Users apply sodium bicarbonate deodorants, store-bought or home-made, to keep underarm odour down and present as clean. It is among the oldest patented deodorant ingredients; trials of this specific use are lacking.

apple-cider-vinegar-for-odour.text: Folk-remedy followers wipe diluted vinegar on the underarms in the belief that its acidity curbs odour. The idea rests on anecdote and has not been tested for this purpose.

chain: Believed to neutralise odour from within
chlorophyll-internal-deodorant.text: Supplement users take chlorophyll or chlorophyllin as an internal deodorant for body, breath and waste odour. Human evidence for body odour specifically is essentially absent, so the appearance link rests on belief and anecdote.

chain: Claimed change in sweat or bacteria
zinc-for-body-odor.text: Supplement and appearance communities circulate the idea that taking zinc orally cuts body odour. Zinc is studied for deficiency, and the sources consulted give no trial support for this odour use.

probiotics-for-body-odor.text: Some users take probiotics on the theory that the gut microbiome shapes how a person smells. Research links gut bacteria to systemic malodour, but human trials of probiotics for body odour were not found.

fruit-and-veg-smell-diet.text: Users eat more fruit and vegetables hoping to make their natural scent more pleasant. A study of men associated higher intake with sweat rated floral, fruity and sweet, with the effect described as mild.

cutting-red-meat-for-smell.text: Users cut red meat in the belief that it makes their body odour more attractive to others. A controlled two-week study in men reportedly rated sweat from the meat diet as less pleasant and more intense; the evidence base is small.

chain: Fewer sulfur compounds in breath and skin
cutting-garlic-and-onion.text: Users skip garlic and onion to avoid lingering breath and skin odour. Sulfur compounds such as allyl methyl sulfide are documented in breath and can persist for up to two days; direct trials on body odour are limited.

cutting-alcohol-for-smell.text: People in appearance and grooming circles cut alcohol in the belief that sweat, breath and body odour become less noticeable. The idea rests on anecdote, with no dedicated studies behind it.

carnivore-diet-smell.text: Carnivore dieters report changes in body odour, with some describing a milder scent and others a stronger or fishy one. The reports are anecdotal and no one has measured the effect.

fish-odor-syndrome-choline-restriction.text: People with trimethylaminuria, a rare condition that gives sweat and breath a fishy smell, discuss choline restriction as one dietary approach. It is used in medically supervised management of the condition rather than as a general grooming tactic.

chain: Odour and residue removed from fabric
Clothes smell fresh on the body
washing-clothes-properly.text: Users launder clothes carefully so garments do not hold odour, dirt or stains, which keeps their overall presentation clean. Fresh-smelling, well-kept fabric is an immediately noticeable part of grooming.

chain: Sanitiser or strip wash on gym kit
laundry-sanitiser-and-strip-washing.text: Gym-goers use laundry sanitisers and heavy strip washes to get persistent odour out of sports clothing. Results are described through popular anecdotes, with no dedicated studies.

chain: Merino fabric worn next to skin
wool-and-merino-clothes.text: Users wear merino wool as a fabric said to resist odour, so clothes stay fresh between washes. The claim is popular in appearance and grooming discussions and untested in the sources reviewed.

cedar-shoe-inserts.text: Users place cedar shoe trees in footwear between wearings to limit shoe and foot odour and keep shoes in shape. Cedar is commonly said to absorb moisture and add its own scent; no trials on odour exist.

foot-powder.text: Users dust foot powder onto feet and into shoes to keep them dry and cut odour as part of a grooming routine. Some formulations add antifungal or deodorant agents; evidence is indirect.

showering-twice-daily.text: Appearance-focused users shower morning and evening, or after exercise, to control body odour and keep skin and hair clean. It is a common habit, and the twice-daily frequency itself has not been studied.

scent-layering-body-wash-lotion-fragranc.text: Users stack matching body wash, lotion and fragrance so their scent builds and lasts longer through the day. The fragrance industry promotes versions of the practice; its effect on longevity is untested.

chain: Others link the scent to you
fragrance-signature-scent.text: Users adopt a single signature fragrance as a memorability and personal-branding tool, so others associate the scent with them. The idea is popular in appearance communities and untested.

hair-perfume-hair-mist.text: Users spray hair mist as a lighter alternative to applying perfume on skin, leaving a scent in the hair. Grooming communities describe it as a way to add a scent trail; no studies cover it.

chain: Scented oil or balm on beard
beard-oil-and-balm-scent.text: Beard owners apply scented oils and balms to keep facial hair soft and manageable, sometimes in place of cologne. The scent and softer look are noticeable right away; no clinical research backs further claims.

fragrance-clones-dupes-zara.text: Online fragrance communities discuss budget brands such as Zara as sources of scents resembling expensive designer releases. They are popular for price, and no formal research compares them with the originals.

chain: Find a scent that suits you
niche-perfume-sample-decants.text: Fragrance buyers use decants, small vials of perfume, to test pricey niche scents before committing to a full bottle. It is a shopping practice that supports choosing a scent, with no appearance research.

sauvage-bleu-de-chanel-compliment-getter.text: Fragrance communities name Dior Sauvage and Bleu de Chanel as compliment getters, scents said to draw positive comments. The compliment claims are anecdotal.

fragrance-reddit-r-fragrance-blind-buys.text: Fragrance shoppers use communities such as r/fragrance for recommendations and buy scents unsmelled. It is a shopping habit for choosing a fragrance to wear; no research covers it.

oud-and-amber-middle-eastern-fragrances.text: Fragrance fans choose oud and amber scents from Middle Eastern perfumery for a rich, distinctive smell. Oud is a traditional base note, and much oud in stores is synthetic.

attar-oils-alcohol-free-perfume.text: Users wear attar, a traditional concentrated perfume oil, as an alcohol-free alternative to colognes. It appears in looksmaxxing and grooming discussions as a scent option, with no appearance research behind it.

chain: Vitamin C and zinc on underarms
vitamin-c-and-zinc-pit-routine.text: Grooming circles discuss an informal underarm routine using topical or dietary vitamin C and zinc to manage odour. It is described as anecdotal, and no published studies of this routine were located.

dermatologist-referral-for-bromhidrosis.text: Users with persistent body odour, often linked to heavy underarm sweating, raise seeing a clinician to check for hyperhidrosis or metabolic causes. The aim is a cleaner natural scent through treating the cause.

tea-tree-oil-body-wash.text: Users choose tea tree oil body wash as a natural antibacterial cleanser for body odour and body acne. Lab antibacterial activity is shown, while trials for odour or looks are absent.
